sections.section_name: Section B - Theory Short Answer Concepts

questions.question_text: Define 'Portraiture' and explain one key element to remember when portraying a person's face. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Portraiture is the art of drawing or painting a specific person. A key element is accurately measuring the proportions and spacing between the eyes, nose, and mouth.

questions.question_text: What is the difference between a melody (Raaga) and rhythm (Taal) in Indian music? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Raaga refers to the melodic framework created using a specific sequence of musical notes (swaras), whereas Taal is the structured rhythmic time cycle or beat pattern that accompanies it.

questions.question_text: How can music effectively express different human emotions? Give one example. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Music expresses emotions through changes in tempo, volume, and note combinations. For example, a slow tempo with soft, minor notes often evokes feelings of sadness or deep peace.

questions.question_text: Describe the technique of 'Origami' and mention the material used for it. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Origami is the traditional Japanese art of paper folding. It transforms a single flat, square sheet of paper into a finished 3D sculpture without using any cuts or glue.

questions.question_text: What role do wind instruments play in a musical performance, and give two examples. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Wind instruments produce sound by blowing air into them, adding continuous melodic lines to performances. Two common examples are the flute (bansuri) and the shehnai.

sections.section_name: Section C - Practical Tasks: Composition & Observation

questions.question_text: Draw a nature study of a small leafy branch with at least two flowers. Apply appropriate watercolor washes to show light and dark tones on the petals. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: Marks are awarded for the organic structural drawing of the branch and petals. Smooth, transparent watercolor application, blending light washes for highlights and darker tones for shadows underneath the leaves, is essential. Neatness and avoiding muddy color mixing will finalize the score.

questions.question_text: Create a well-composed still life drawing of a half-open book alongside a lit candle on a stand. Use charcoal or soft pencils to establish heavy contrast and shadows. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: Evaluators will look for accurate perspective on the open book pages. The glow effect around the candle flame should be created using an eraser. Smooth, bold charcoal shading for the deep background and cast shadows on the table will secure maximum points.

sections.section_name: Section D - Practical Tasks: Applied Design & Messaging

questions.question_text: Design a visually striking poster on the theme 'Water is Life'. Integrate a central graphic representing water conservation and use bold block lettering for the slogan. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: The poster must have a clear, balanced layout within a defined border. The central graphic (like hands holding a water drop or a turning off tap) should be prominent. Marks are awarded for readable, thick block lettering, creative use of blue color palettes, and the overall impact of the conservation message.

questions.question_text: Create a repetitive geometrical border design suitable for a textile print (like a saree border). Use a repeating motif of triangles and circles filled with contrasting poster colors. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: The primary focus is on the precision and mathematical repetition of the geometric motif along a straight horizontal track. Neat application of thick, opaque poster colors without spilling outside the lines is required. Using highly contrasting colors (e.g., yellow and dark blue) to make the pattern pop will earn full marks.
